items.title: Sensex surges over 1,200 points, Nifty reclaims 23,400 as RIL leads rally
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced a significant surge, primarily driven by Reliance Industries which saw an 11.6% increase. Easing crude oil prices and renewed diplomatic talks regarding Iran contributed positively to investor sentiment. The BSE Sensex rose by more than 1,200 points, while the NSE Nifty exceeded the 23,400 mark. Broader market segments, including metals and cement stocks, also experienced noteworthy gains.

items.title: Sebi allows REITs, InvITs to tap overseas investors through depository receipts
items.description: Sebi has established frameworks allowing real estate investment trusts and infrastructure investment trusts to issue foreign currency denominated depository receipts. This initiative enables them to access capital from overseas markets through international exchanges in GIFT City. To issue depository receipts, unitholder approval will be required, with a majority supporting such moves. Certain restrictions and conditions will apply to participating trusts and existing unitholders.

items.title: We will consider the call for review of LTCG tax: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
items.description: "The circumstances have changed and, therefore, the voices of concern are louder,'' she said at a media event, in reference to reports that her administration has received suggestions to review levies on long-term capital gains (LTCG) for overseas investors. "I quite appreciate that. So, I'll consider all this... Our growth is very important, where people are putting their very best, we are able to see sustained 7(%)-plus growth.''

items.title: D-Street poised for positive start as GIFT Nifty signals gains
items.description: Indian equity markets enjoyed a rally, spurred by robust buying in major stocks such as Reliance Industries. Analysts pegged immediate support for Nifty at 23,200, with resistance encountered at 23,500 and 23,700. Foreign portfolio investors were active buyers, netting Rs 3,115 crore, while domestic institutional investors offloaded shares worth Rs 392 crore. Meanwhile, the rupee dipped by 10 paise to close at 94.

items.title: Stocks in news: ITC, Marico, SBI, Yatra Online, NSE, Container Corp and Sun Pharma
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks experienced gains, with Nifty nearing the 23,500 resistance level and strong corporate earnings reported. ITC faced a decline in consolidated net profit, impacted by the cigarette business, despite revenue growth. Marico saw a significant rise in net profit and expanding EBITDA margins during the quarter. Container Corporation of India reported a subdued performance with a slight decline in net profit compared to last year.

items.title: RIL shares surge 11.6% on strong Q2 earnings; analysts see further upside
items.description: Reliance Industries has seen an impressive 11.6% surge in stock price, following quarterly earnings that exceeded expectations. This remarkable rise represents the company's most significant increase in over six years. Analysts are optimistic about future growth, crediting this success to strong performance in the O2C sector and increased institutional buying. Brokerage firms predict potential earnings upgrades will further boost stock valuation.

items.title: FPI holding hits multi-year lows in 70% of top 100 Indian companies
items.description: Foreign investors have significantly reduced their holdings in nearly 70% of India's leading companies in recent years. Major firms, including banks and IT sectors, are seeing foreign ownership decline to multi-decade lows. This decrease in foreign investments mirrors diminished expectations for growth in India relative to other global markets. Although some companies experience slight increases in foreign ownership, they still remain at historical lows.

items.title: Stock Radar: Coforge stock hits fresh record high in October; will the rally continue in November 2026?
items.description: Coforge Ltd has achieved a fresh record high and has shown strong growth in recent weeks. The stock’s upward momentum suggests potential targets above 2,200 levels in the next few weeks. Analysts recommend a buy-on-dips strategy, maintaining a strict stop loss at 1,810. Technical indicators indicate sustained strength and positive momentum in the stock's performance. Investors are encouraged to consider these positions as the market evolves.

items.title: Aditya Birla Lifestyle bets on festive demand
items.description: The company, which owns brands such as Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter England, reported flat like-for-like sales growth in September, against 5.3% for the second quarter of FY27. The slowdown comes just as the full impact of price increases begins to flow through in the December quarter, making consumer acceptance and discounting critical to sustaining growth.

items.title: Institutional investors step up bets on private credit as insurers, pension funds and DFIs back new funds
items.description: Institutional investors are now allocating more funds to private credit, significantly from insurance companies and pension funds. Neo Alternative Asset Managers has seen its second fund receive 22-25% contributions from these investors. Ascertis Credit's fourth fund also attracted commitments exceeding $700 million from multiple institutional investors. With increased interest in private credit, annual investment opportunities are now estimated around ₹1 lakh crore.

items.title: A month after RBI’s rate hike, banks start raising deposit rates as liquidity shrinks, Bank of India the latest to move
items.description: Domestic banks are beginning to increase their deposit rates due to shrinking liquidity conditions in the market. Bank of India recently announced a rate hike on deposits for various maturities, including a special 500-day option. This decision reflects the growing cost of deposits in the banking system as demand for credit rises. Banking system liquidity has significantly decreased from its peak in early September.

items.title: MFs cut stakes in 8 smallcap stocks after two quarters of buying; shares tumble up to 30% in 3 months
items.description: An analysis of mutual fund (MF) shareholding trends across BSE small-cap stocks over the past three quarters reveals a notable shift in institutional ownership. During the September 2026 quarter, mutual funds reduced their holdings in 79 stocks, reversing the accumulation trend seen over the previous two consecutive quarters, December 2025 to March 2026 and March 2026 to June 2026.Most of these stocks have delivered negative returns over the past three months. In fact, 39 stocks have declined by more than 10% during this period. Among them, we have highlighted 8 major laggards that have corrected between 25% and 30% in the past three months, even as mutual funds reduced their stakes after increasing their holdings over the previous two quarters. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: NSE International Exchange begins 23.5-hour trading, extends market access across global time zones
items.description: NSE International Exchange has introduced a 23.5-hour trading schedule, providing near-continuous market access across Asian, European and American time zones. The extended window aims to help global investors respond to international developments while strengthening GIFT City’s position as a global financial hub.

items.title: GRSE shares jump 9% after signing Rs 32,000 crore Indian Navy contract for five next-generation corvettes
items.description: GRSE shares surged nearly 9% after securing a Rs 32,000-crore Indian Navy contract to build five Next Generation Corvettes. The nine-year project will strengthen indigenous defence manufacturing, enhance maritime capabilities and reinforce GRSE's warship-building position, adding significantly to its order book and long-term business prospects.

items.title: 4 reasons why Reliance Industries shares can rally after Monday magic sparked historic 12% surge
items.description: Reliance Industries shares surged, their biggest single-day gain since April 2020, adding nearly Rs 2 lakh crore to the company's market capitalisation after strong Q2 results. Despite remaining down over 17% in 2026, analysts see further upside potential, citing positive fundamental and technical cues.

items.title: Angel One, CDSL, BSE, other capital market stocks jump up to 8%. 3 reasons behind the rally
items.description: Capital market stocks rallied up to 8% as hopes of LTCG tax relief, renewed FII buying and a broader market recovery lifted investor sentiment. The Nifty Capital Markets index climbed over 3% to a seven-week high.

items.title: Uncertainty is certain: India is resilient and will emerge stronger
items.description: Despite global uncertainty, India remains well placed to weather economic and market disruptions, supported by resilient growth, deeper domestic capital markets and rising private investment. Stronger institutions, infrastructure spending and emerging industries could further reinforce the country’s long-term prospects.

items.title: KRBL shares rally 9% after Q2 net profit jumps 51% YoY
items.description: KRBL shares jumped nearly 9% after the company reported a 51% rise in second-quarter profit, supported by strong domestic sales and improved operating performance. Revenue increased 14%, while EBITDA climbed sharply, reinforcing positive momentum in the stock.

items.title: Only 3.2% of working Indians trade stocks. Why Morgan Stanley likes NSE
items.description: Morgan Stanley has initiated coverage of NSE with an overweight rating and a price target of Rs 2,315, citing its dominant market share, strong liquidity and India’s underpenetrated capital markets. The brokerage expects revenue and normalised profit to grow at 15% annually between FY27 and FY29. It sees long-term growth opportunities but flags regulatory changes and market-share losses as key risks.

items.title: Record-breaking FII selling may have peaked, says Nomura. Why the Nifty target could rise
items.description: FIIs may be nearing the end of their record selling spree in Indian equities as outflows ease, earnings beat expectations and valuations fall below post-pandemic averages, according to Nomura. Foreign investors sold around $8.8 billion since September 15, although the pace has moderated. Meanwhile, companies in Nomura’s BSE 200+ universe reported 34% year-on-year profit growth, beating consensus estimates by 18%.

items.title: US midterm elections today: Can Trump’s pain be Dalal Street’s gain? Analysts estimate impact in 3 possible scenarios
items.description: The United States will hold crucial midterm elections that could significantly alter the balance of power in Congress. Analysts are focusing on potential scenarios that could emerge based on whether the Democrats or Republicans hold the majority. These outcomes may impact critical issues such as tariffs, immigration, foreign relations, and even oil prices.

items.title: Trident shares rally 13% after Q2 net profit jumps 93% to Rs 175 crore; firm plans Rs 4,650 crore capex
items.description: Trident shares rallied 13% after the company reported a 93.1% year-on-year rise in Q2 FY27 net profit to Rs 175.50 crore. Improved EBITDA and margins supported earnings growth, while the company announced a Rs 4,650-crore capacity expansion and modernisation programme.

items.title: Diwali stocks by Motilal Oswal: Eternal, Adani Ports among 10 stocks with upside of up to 40%. See full list
items.description: Motilal Oswal said Samvat 2083 has begun on a cautious note, with an external energy shock weighing on market sentiment despite the resilience of the domestic economy. The West Asia conflict has kept Brent crude prices above $100 per barrel, pushing CPI inflation to 5.54% in September and prompting a 25 basis points repo rate hike to 5.50%. However, Motilal Oswal expects FY27 to mark a return to double-digit earnings growth, with Nifty earnings per share (EPS) projected to rise 16% and 14% year-on-year in FY27 and FY28, respectively, compared with 5% growth in FY26. Here are 10 stocks the brokerage is bullish on.

items.title: Smallcap stocks to buy this Diwali! 5 stocks with upside potential of up to 37%. Do you own any?
items.description: Mirae Asset Sharekhan says the correction has improved risk-reward materially but valuations are not uniformly inexpensive and there are pockets where valuations have corrected much more than the earnings outlook suggests. The Nifty 50’s one-year forward multiple at ~17x is lower than the 10-year average. This makes the next year a stock-picker’s market, where businesses with strong fundamentals, earnings visibility and reasonable valuations should be better-placed to generate returns. Here are 5 smallcap stocks the brokerage is bullish on?

items.title: LTCG abolition may cost just Rs 40,000–50,000 crore, SBI estimates show
items.description: SBI Research estimates that abolishing long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax would cost the government just Rs 40,000–50,000 crore in FY27, far below the Rs 1.3 lakh crore collected in FY25. Weaker stock market returns and sustained foreign investor outflows have significantly reduced expected collections, suggesting the move may not derail the government's fiscal consolidation plans.

items.title: ideaForge shares jump 7% as firm swings to profit in Q2, revenue soars 124% YoY
items.description: ideaForge shares surged over 7% after the company reported a turnaround to a Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 6.46 crore, while revenue jumped 124% year-on-year to Rs 91.29 crore. Improved operating performance and new defence technology milestones boosted investor interest.

items.title: IndiGo, Indian Oil and other crude-sensitive stocks rally up to 4% as oil dips below $105/bbl. Where are prices headed?
items.description: Crude-sensitive stocks such as IndiGo, BPCL, HPCL and Indian Oil rallied up to 4% as oil prices declined for a second consecutive session amid US-Iran peace talks. Upstream stocks ONGC and Oil India, however, fell up to 2%. Lower crude prices typically benefit downstream companies by easing input costs and supporting refining and marketing margins.

items.title: Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running case
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has imposed a total penalty of Rs 40 lakh on four entities. This penalty includes fines on Woodstock Broking and Marfatia Stock Broking for front-running trades. The investigation spanned from April 1, 2021, to March 31, 2022, involving these entities. Evidence indicated that brokers facilitated these trades by providing necessary infrastructure and assistance.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
items.description: Indian equities rallied nearly 2%, with Sensex gaining 1,225 points and Nifty rising 370 points. Falling crude prices, renewed FII buying, resilient earnings and expectations of LTCG tax changes boosted sentiment, adding nearly Rs 4 lakh crore to market capitalisation.

items.title: Indian Hotels Company among 6 stocks that hit 52-week highs and rallied up to 16% in a month
items.description: On Friday, the benchmark Sensex climbed 1,225 points to settle at 76,917. Riding the market rally, six stocks from the BSE 200 index hit fresh 52-week highs, touching their highest price levels in the past 12 months. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the last year and may indicate heightened market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Motilal Oswal Financial Services announces leadership rejig; appoints new heads across businesses
items.description: Motilal Oswal Financial Services announced major leadership changes across alternatives, retail broking and private wealth businesses. The reshuffle coincides with strong Q2 performance, with operating PAT rising 29% year-on-year to Rs 718 crore.

items.title: For investors with a 3- to 5-year horizon: 5 mid-cap stocks from different sectors with upside potential of more than 19%
items.description: A development worth noting is that there was net FII buying in five of the last six trading sessions. But it is still tentative, and cannot be declared as a reversal of the selling trend of the past few months. While indications are that they are favouring large-cap stocks, there are bargains to be had in the mid-cap space for the discerning investor.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A capital markets stock for 6.75% gain, a large-cap commodities platform for a rise of 7%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Market wrap:  BSE, Nestle India, Power Grid, SBI top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Tuesday
items.description: Indian markets extended gains as the Sensex surged 1,225 points and Nifty climbed 370 points. Falling crude prices, softer US Treasury yields and FII buying boosted sentiment, with FMCG and realty stocks leading the broad-based rally.

items.title: FPIs pour Rs 21,715 crore into Indian stocks in 10 days; is record sell-off finally reversing?
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors infused $2.29 billion into Indian equities over 10 days, signalling improving sentiment. Strong corporate earnings, attractive valuations and potential LTCG tax relief could revive foreign inflows, while crude oil prices remain a key risk.

items.title: R&D-focused stocks deliver over 23% annualised returns in five years, outperform NSE 500: Monarch AIF
items.description: Indian companies increasing R&D spending outperformed the NSE 500 TRI over five years, delivering 23.5% average annualised returns. Businesses combining strong research growth with higher R&D intensity achieved 32.5%, highlighting innovation's growing importance for investors.

items.title: Emcure Pharma shares jump 7% after Q2 profit rises 29% YoY to Rs 325 crore
items.description: Emcure Pharmaceuticals shares rose up to 7.3% after the company reported a 29.3% year-on-year increase in Q2 FY27 profit to Rs 325.1 crore. Revenue grew 24.3%, while EBITDA rose 30.9%, supported by strong international business growth.

items.title: Bonus issue alert! Choice International to reward shareholders with 1:1 bonus shares. Check details
items.description: Choice International has approved a 1:1 bonus issue, its first such corporate action in two years. Under the proposal, shareholders will receive one bonus share for every share held on the record date, which will be announced later. The move will double the number of outstanding shares without changing the company’s market capitalisation, while potentially improving stock liquidity and affordability.
